authoritative_for: EMT owns incident tracking, retained email exchanges, Nucleus correlation, frozen outgoing mail, worker admission and its installation.
not_authoritative_for: Clockwork owns scheduling halts and notification claims. Nucleus owns agent execution and activity. Email owns transport and credentials. Products own intervention results.

covers: EMT incident diagnosis, email-directed interventions, exchange inspection, mail submission, configuration, worker, schedule, maintenance and installation operations.
excludes: Help/version, external sender authentication, provider deletion, final inbox delivery and product-domain recovery implementations.

shared_access_and_trust: Current-user private service. Explicit activation authorizes incident diagnosis and mail. Recognized replies authorize one-off interventions; sender verification is deferred. Agents use local execution and unrestricted current-user filesystem, process, local socket, and network access without Codex sandbox restrictions or approval prompts.
shared_privacy_and_retention: Retains incidents and correspondence without automatic deletion. Job IDs point to Nucleus activity; no operation ledger or tool-output mirror. Providers retain separate copies.

CLI usage recording requires a nonempty `CODEX_THREAD_ID`. Chancery's private journal records command identity, time, and thread ID, not arguments, output, or outcomes. Internal product calls are excluded. Recording errors do not change command results.
compatibility_and_retirement: EMT release and schema one are independent of provider contracts. Exact pending requests and frozen emails survive restarts. Unsupported schema fails. Installation does not activate work.
operational_limits: One agent assignment at a time, one 100-incident feed page and four 100-message receiving pages per pass. Five-minute diagnosis and fifteen-minute reply deadlines. No timer or delivery latency guarantee.
